title: Linking and connected speech
what: pronouncing every word separately instead of linking ('turn_it_off', 'an_apple', 'what do you' as 'whaddya' in casual speech)
summary: Advanced learners often focus on articulating each word distinctly, overlooking the natural flow of connected speech. This can make communication sound less fluid and occasionally impede listener comprehension.
listenFor: Pay attention to whether your words flow together smoothly or if there are noticeable pauses and breaks between them.
drills: Could you tell me about it, if you have a moment?
We need to iron out all the details before we sign off on it.
It's an important issue that affects us all, isn't it?
I often find myself thinking about what it all means.
They're planning to open up a new office in another city.
What are you going to do about it, if anything at all?
She always takes an interest in what her colleagues are working on.
We ought to put an end to this misunderstanding immediately.
He asked if I'd be able to assist him with the upcoming project.
It's a good idea to write it all down, isn't it, for future reference?
